message:
Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, every function has concepts from all four members so nobody owes a concept, and the two weakest functions for depiction are transfer loads to structure and maintain deck appearance. In plain words the physics is settled but the drawing misread the beam and the clamp and the deck ban. No new distant analogy is needed because friction-clamp, lift run and jury and decay analogies are already on the board, what is owed is the viewpoint-relative zone lock with counts.

Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, the numbers reconcile and fit everyday feel and the critical missing quantity is the steel of the beam itself. In plain words damped shake is a small fraction of gravity while bare shake is near body weight and motion fits in a hand, and added steel is about ten people on a crowded deck. Retrofitted 0.67 m/s2 from the crowd build-up simulation (E45) is 0.068 times gravity inside Medium versus bare 8.28 m/s2 from the bare-acceleration calculation (E43) at 0.844 times gravity outside everyday feel, travel 49.4 mm from the free-decay simulation (E17) clears 80 mm stops with sag 74.7 mm from the static-sag calculation (E63) totalling 124 mm from the envelope calculation (E68) about a hand span, and added 7.85 kN from the static-weight calculation (E26) is 1.31 percent from the weight-fraction calculation (E72) of 600 kN live load from the live-load estimate (E30), where 1.31 percent is correct and 0.133 percent from the added-weight check (E71) is kilograms over newtons and is dropped, with 32.9 kN slip per bolt from the slip-resistance calculation (E64) against 13.1 kN demand from the combined-load calculation (E65) including 8.40 kN stop hit from the stop-force calculation (E66), leaving beam plus stop steel unweighed against the 2 percent rule as the uncomputed quantity.

Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, the drawing failure says under-specified topology, not failed physics, and the two not-ready votes are now answered by joint confirmation. In plain words the single beam must read short transverse not long longitudinal, the clamp callout must land on the beam-to-web zone, and nothing extra may sit above the deck. The ordered chain central twin-mass zone to spring-plus-damper zone to single short transverse cross-beam zone to left beam-end-to-girder-web clamp zone and right beam-end-to-girder-web clamp zone to left girder host zone and right girder host zone from the layout sketch (E55) and the transverse clamp sketch (E74) with Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) axes diagonal, High-Strength Friction-Grip (HSFG) bolts only in the two clamp zones, two masses and two spring sets and two dampers and one beam and two girder interfaces with bolt count representative, and zero added items above the deck serviced from below by Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV) with no deck hatch, resolves Bridge Retrofit Engineer on binding jointly confirmed by Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead and Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor on the zero ban confirmed by Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, and accepts Structural Dynamicist and Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead as ready on twin-detuned 0.476 to 0.526 m/s2 from the detuning sweep (E70) and off-antinode 0.75 from the modal effectiveness calculation (E67).

RECORD: Decided twin 400 kg Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) pair on HSFG-clamped transverse cross-beam at midspan antinode below soffit within girder depth with 80 mm stops and crowd acceptance run; numbers that stand are 800 kg total (E13) 7.85 kN (E26) 1.31 percent (E72) 1.83 Hz (E14) 12.0 percent (E15) 6.20 percent effective (E17) 0.67 m/s2 versus 8.28 m/s2 (E45)(E43) 49.4 mm 80 mm 74.7 mm 124 mm (E17)(E63)(E68) 32.9 kN versus 13.1 kN plus 8.40 kN (E64)(E65)(E66); still open are beam-steel weight, re-votes by Bridge Retrofit Engineer and Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor on the zone lock, and the after-build crowd walk-through bench test.

Note on Structural Dynamicist: Tune tolerance and effective damping hold with evidence.
Note on Bridge Retrofit Engineer: Slip margin stands but owed re-vote on joint binding.
Note on Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor: Medium verdict stands but owed re-vote on zero ban.
Note on Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead: Transverse station and from-below access jointly confirm both bans.

My position is not ready, because physics and loads stand but depiction lock and two re-votes plus beam weight are still open.
